nodes.label: FLIR Spinnaker SDK License Agreement
nodes.author: FLIR Systems Inc.
nodes.rationale: Limited, terminable, non-transferable licence to use the SDK only with listed FLIR cameras you own and images derived from them; no redistribution or reverse engineering. Free/open-source components of the SDK are governed solely by their own licences, not this agreement.

nodes.label: Transport-Layer Stream Buffer Settings
nodes.rationale: These live in the transport-layer stream nodemap, which user sets do not cover, so the app must own them and there is no invariant 7 tension. OldestFirst back-pressures rather than discarding, which is what a recorder wants; NewestOnly silently drops and is right only for a live viewer. 10 buffers is ~0.33 s of slack at 30 fps, 64 gives ~2 s.

nodes.label: UserSet1 Has Never Been Configured
nodes.rationale: Default, UserSet0 and UserSet1 are identical factory defaults; nothing in this repo has ever executed UserSetSave. So config.toml's user_set = "UserSet1" loads factory settings and preflight correctly fails every [camera_verify] check that matters.

nodes.label: Blackfly S BFS-U3-04S2C (serial 22514545)
nodes.rationale: The measured record of the rig camera; when it and a design document disagree, the measurement wins. The trailing C is colour, and the cp310 PySpin wheel is why the acquisition PC is pinned to Python 3.10.

nodes.label: 60-Second Pipeline Measurement Under Load
nodes.rationale: 3960 frames in 60.0 s at 66.0 fps free-running with zero drops, zero incomplete, zero frame-ID gaps, monotonic hardware timestamps, h264_qsv output at 5.6 MB/min. Sustaining more than double the configured 30 fps is the real evidence for invariants 3 and 10.

nodes.label: 720 × 540 Sensor Correction (not 1280 × 720)
nodes.rationale: The old '720p60' note was a misreading of '720 × 540'; every derived figure was wrong-high. Corrected: raw rate 11.7 MB/s not ~25, pre-roll ~23 MB not ~55, storage far below the ~37 MB/min estimate.

nodes.label: Auto-Exposure / Auto-Gain Covariance Problem
nodes.rationale: ExposureAuto and GainAuto re-tune continuously as the rat descends, so image appearance covaries with the very thing DLC is trained to locate. Read 14999 µs on one probe and 1002 µs on another; the problem is not that 15 ms is long, it is that the value is not under anyone's control.

nodes.label: Read-Only Nodes = Spinnaker Parameter Lock
nodes.rationale: UserSetLoad/UserSetSave/PixelFormat/Width/Height going RO together means another Spinnaker session has the camera latched, not a firmware fault. DeviceAccessStatus, StreamIsGrabbing and TLParamsLocked are host-side state for the probing process and cannot observe a different process — the original diagnosis leaned on them and was wrong. The reliable test is whether the whole cluster is RO at once.

nodes.label: Chunk Data Off As Shipped
nodes.rationale: FrameID and Timestamp chunks and ChunkModeActive are all False as shipped. TimestampIncrement reads 1000, so the counter is 1 µs resolution expressed in nanoseconds and needs no scaling — but read the node at open() rather than hardcoding it, since it is a per-model property.

nodes.rationale: Must be idempotent because preflight opens the camera and leaves it open, then CaptureController.start() opens it again. Caches frame_rate from AcquisitionResultingFrameRate, not AcquisitionFrameRate, which is a ceiling (66.12 vs 199.93 on this camera).

nodes.label: Checkpoint A10 — SpinnakerCamera Implementation
nodes.rationale: Code complete and streaming (60 s / 3960 frames, zero drops); remaining failures all trace to one cause — UserSet1 still holds factory defaults — so verification is blocked on SpinView rig configuration, not on code.

nodes.label: Checkpoint A9.5 — Camera Backend Schema
nodes.rationale: Rewrote the A9 plan against real hardware: backend self-reports geometry/format/rate, preflight asserts config against all of them, [camera_verify] table moves to config, HARDWARE.md records the measured camera.

nodes.label: Storage Management and Transfer Staging
nodes.rationale: GB free is not actionable mid-session, so the readout is estimated remaining recording time from measured bitrate. Remote is a generic mounted path / rsync / robocopy target, never an institution-specific system. Purge requires explicit confirmation after verified transfer.

nodes.label: UserSet1 Camera Settings Profile
nodes.rationale: Camera-onboard profile configured in SpinView and loaded at startup; keeping image-formation settings on the camera rather than in the app is what makes invariant 7 enforceable.

nodes.label: Invariant 7 — No Camera Configuration UI
nodes.rationale: Governs image-formation parameters (exposure, gain, ROI, gamma, trigger) that change what the science looks like; the app refuses to record against a wrongly-configured camera rather than silently fixing one. Carve-out: chunk data and transport-layer stream buffers are data-integrity settings the app owns and logs.

nodes.label: tomli Backport for Python 3.10
nodes.rationale: tomllib is stdlib only from 3.11, and the acquisition PC runs 3.10 because its PySpin wheel is cp310-only — so the Python pin propagates into how config is loaded.

nodes.label: A9.5 · UserSet verification list resolved by measurement
nodes.norm_label: a9.5 · userset verification list resolved by measurement
nodes.rationale: Probing showed the camera boots into factory Default with ExposureAuto/GainAuto Continuous, GammaEnable True at 0.80 and AcquisitionFrameRateEnable False — exactly the settings whose drift corrupts DLC training data, so those became the verification list. Lives in config.toml [camera_verify] rather than code constants so a second rig can differ without a source change.

nodes.label: A9.5 · chunk-data enablement vs. invariant 7
nodes.rationale: Chose to have the app enable chunk data idempotently at open() and amended invariant 7 explicitly rather than leaving code quietly contradicting the document. The stricter alternative (require it in UserSet1, hard-fail preflight) fails closed on a setting nobody would think to check, and its failure mode — a session blocked at the rig with an animal in hand — is worse.

nodes.label: A9.5 · Mono8 vs colour pixel format
nodes.norm_label: a9.5 · mono8 vs colour pixel format
nodes.rationale: Chose Mono8 on a colour sensor: DLC gains nothing from colour for this task, Mono8 is a third of the bytes on a disk-constrained machine, and debayering costs host CPU on a PC with no usable GPU. Recorded honestly that Mono8 here is luma from the Bayer mosaic, so slightly softer than a true mono sensor. Flagged as a scientific call rather than silently settled.

nodes.rationale: Abstract interface reporting resolution, pixel_format, frame_rate, verify_settings and incomplete_frame_count so preflight can compare what the hardware actually does against what config intends.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera Backend
nodes.rationale: Real hardware path via PySpin, deliberately built after the mock path was complete and tested.

nodes.label: spinnaker-python Wheel Name
nodes.rationale: The pip distribution name is `spinnaker-python` even though the import name is `PySpin`, so querying pip for `pyspin` is a false negative.

nodes.label: PySpin Exception Translation Convention
nodes.rationale: Every public method wraps PySpin calls and re-raises as CameraError so callers never import or catch PySpin-specific exceptions; `import PySpin` stays inside methods so the module remains importable with no SDK installed.

nodes.label: Invariant 2 — Mock Backend Is First-Class
nodes.rationale: Zero-hardware runnability is what makes an unattended build verifiable; it also forces `import PySpin` to stay inside methods rather than at module scope.

nodes.label: PySpin Is Vendor-Distributed, Not on PyPI
nodes.norm_label: pyspin is vendor-distributed, not on pypi
nodes.rationale: The wheel must match your Python/OS and comes from the Spinnaker SDK download after installing the SDK itself; it is only required for SpinnakerCamera, since MockCamera and all tests run without it.

nodes.label: Zero-Dependency Testing Requirement
nodes.rationale: No test may require DLC, PySpin, CUDA or a network mount — that is what makes an unattended run verifiable. The bounded-queue drop behaviour, the trial state machine guards, and the kinematics ground-truth recovery are the three places tests earn their keep.

nodes.label: Acquisition-Side Cross-Repo Contract
nodes.rationale: Any field name/type/meaning change requires updating shared/schema/ and the analysis repo's manifest stage in the same commit, plus a schema_version bump.

nodes.label: Session Directory and Filename Convention
nodes.rationale: t<NNN> alone guarantees uniqueness; HHMM disambiguates repeat sessions on the same animal same day. The optional <view> token exists because DeepLabCut flattens folder structure on import, so filenames must stand alone.

nodes.label: Stage 0 · build_manifest
nodes.rationale: Reads session_metadata.json and trials.csv from archive session dirs into manifest.parquet, one row per trial × view. This manifest is the spine — every later stage queries it rather than crawling the filesystem.

nodes.label: Stage 9 · report
nodes.rationale: Group-level aggregation, statistics and figures reading only trial_summary.parquet and kinematics_long.parquet — a clean, testable input contract, but in tension with what 'group-level' implies since neither file carries animal_id or project_name.

nodes.label: Trial UID — Primary Join Key
nodes.rationale: Stable deterministic string keying trial+view, used as the join key everywhere. Its compound form {animal_id}_{project_name}_{date}_{initials}_{view}_t{NNN} is not safely reversible because component fields can contain underscores.

nodes.label: shared/schema Cross-App Contract
nodes.rationale: session_metadata.json, trials.csv and timestamp sidecars are defined once with a schema_version so divergence between the two apps cannot surface as a crash on real data months later.

nodes.label: A0 Comes First — Contract Before Apps
nodes.norm_label: a0 comes first — contract before apps
nodes.rationale: Schemas are defined once with a schema_version and imported by both sides because divergence surfaces as a crash on real data months from now. Round-trip tests (acquisition writes a synthetic session, analysis reads it into a manifest) are the contract's proof and exist from A0 onward.

nodes.label: A9.5 · camera settings not recorded in session metadata
nodes.norm_label: a9.5 · camera settings not recorded in session metadata
nodes.rationale: Left shared/schema/ untouched rather than extending CameraInfo with measured values, because any field change is a schema_version bump requiring a coordinated two-repo commit — widening the blast radius past what this acquisition-local pass was scoped to. The change is additive when it happens and worth doing deliberately alongside the analysis repo.

nodes.label: B5 · report stage cannot group by animal
nodes.norm_label: b5 · report stage cannot group by animal
nodes.rationale: Parsing trial_uid back into fields is fragile in general, not just at the edges — animal_id, project_name and initials are free-ish text that can themselves contain underscores. Built aggregate_overall() and aggregate_by_keypoint() against exactly the declared inputs; the clean later fix is adding animal_id/project_name columns to TrialSummaryRow, an additive change.

nodes.label: Reason-Code Hotkey Flagging
nodes.rationale: Every trial is valid by default and annotation is subtractive and never blocking; flags toggle, are not mutually exclusive, and target the recording trial if active else the most recent one so late annotation still works.

nodes.label: Stage 1 · qc_gate
nodes.rationale: Adds included (bool) and exclusion_reason from config-driven rules (experimenter flags non-empty, dropped-frame rate, implausible duration, achieved_fps deviation). Never drops rows, so exclusions stay auditable and reversible.

nodes.label: PoseProvider Protocol (stubbed only)
nodes.rationale: send_frame / get_latest_pose (non-blocking) wired into the capture path with a NullPoseProvider, so it can later be swapped for network-offload or on-device Jetson inference. TriggerService.on_pose is a no-op hook for future closed-loop use; no actual inference is implemented.

nodes.label: Invariant 8 — Trial Stop Is a Pluggable Predicate
nodes.norm_label: invariant 8 — trial stop is a pluggable predicate
nodes.rationale: Stop is keypress-driven today and pose-driven later, so it must never be welded into a Qt event handler.

nodes.label: Invariant 2 — Undistort Coordinates, Never Video
nodes.rationale: Re-encoding video to undistort is lossy, slow, and destroys the archive's write-once property; calibration is applied to pose output post-hoc instead. Lens distortion correction is mandatory because anything distorting apparent velocity as a function of height is a first-order threat to the hypothesis.

nodes.label: Invariant 3 — QC Marks, Never Deletes
nodes.rationale: Excluded trials stay in the manifest with an included boolean and exclusion_reason so exclusions are auditable and reversible.

nodes.label: opencv-python-headless for Coordinate Undistortion Only
nodes.rationale: Pinned headless and annotated 'never touches video' so the dependency itself encodes invariant 2.

nodes.label: Anticipated Drift Paths
nodes.rationale: Named in advance as invariant violations: unbounded frame queue, PySpin before the mock path, QC dropping rows instead of marking included=False, undistorting video instead of coordinates, hardcoded thresholds, welding the stop condition into the Qt handler, GUI stylesheets, silently bridging long interpolation gaps.

nodes.label: A3 · no distinct auto_flag for predicate stops
nodes.norm_label: a3 · no distinct auto_flag for predicate stops
nodes.rationale: Inventing an auto_flag vocabulary entry before any real predicate exists risks the analysis QC gate being built against a code that will not match what a real pose-driven condition needs to express. auto_flags is already an open string set, so adding one later is one line, not a schema change.

nodes.label: Stage 2 · calibration
nodes.rationale: Intrinsics only — camera matrix and distortion coefficients per camera_serial and calibration epoch, valid until the camera is moved or refocused. Pixel→mm scale is derived per-video from pole landmarks at the kinematics stage, not here. A trial with no valid epoch is a QC failure, not a silent pass.

nodes.label: Archive / Cache / Derived Data Tiering
nodes.rationale: Video is huge and everything derived from it is small, and inference is the only stage needing raw video — so CRSP is a write-once archive, the local cache is transient and sized for one batch, and derived artifacts are versioned. Nothing downstream of inference requires CRSP or a GPU.

nodes.label: Stage 7 · infer
nodes.rationale: The only stage that needs raw video: pull from archive to local cache, analyze_videos, write pose .h5, verify, delete the local copy. Resumable by skipping trials whose pose exists with matching snapshot ID and config hash. This is the pipeline bottleneck, so per-trial throughput is logged.

nodes.label: Stage 8 · kinematics
nodes.rationale: Order matters: likelihood filter → gap interpolation (gaps longer than max_gap_frames stay NaN, never silently bridged) → smoothing → undistort coordinates → pole coordinate frame from landmarks → height normalisation → mm scaling. Pole landmark drift mid-trial means the camera was bumped and flags the trial.

nodes.label: RTX 5070 Ti / Blackwell sm_120 cu128 Requirement
nodes.norm_label: rtx 5070 ti / blackwell sm_120 cu128 requirement
nodes.rationale: PyTorch 2.6 has no Blackwell kernels and will fail or fall back silently, so torch must come from the cu128 index-URL wheel. The CUDA version nvidia-smi reports is the driver ceiling, not what PyTorch uses — verify with torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0) expecting (12, 0).

nodes.label: DeepLabCut and torch Deliberately Excluded
nodes.rationale: Stages 3/5/6/7 are scaffolded not implemented, so installing DLC/torch is not needed to run B1–B6. On the analysis PC torch must come from the cu128 index-url — never `pip install torch` plain.

nodes.label: B4/B6/B7 Checkpoint Ordering Gap
nodes.rationale: Kinematics (B4) is checkpointed before infer (B7) but structurally depends on stage 7's pose output, and B6 wires per-stage CLI commands in between — so at no point in the prescribed build order can `python -m pipeline kinematics` have real or placeholder input data to read.

nodes.label: B6 · kinematics CLI stage not wired
nodes.norm_label: b6 · kinematics cli stage not wired
nodes.rationale: Fabricating a DLC-shaped .h5 would mean inventing stage 7's output contract under time pressure purely to unblock stage 8's CLI wiring — speculative plumbing built to satisfy a checkpoint rather than a requirement. Registered kinematics as present-but-unimplemented; wiring it into STAGE_REGISTRY later is one additive Stage(...) entry.

nodes.label: B1 · stage 2 calibration has no checkpoint
nodes.norm_label: b1 · stage 2 calibration has no checkpoint
nodes.rationale: Building an unassigned stage is scope expansion the overnight prompt explicitly warns against, and checkerboard calibration needs real images — there is no synthetic-data path the way B4's kinematics core has one, so it would not be unattended-buildable even if in scope. CalibrationRecord defines the data shape so B4 and a future calibration stage share one contract.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.start_streaming()
nodes.rationale: Where invariant 3's 'not polling' is earned: subclass PySpin.ImageEventHandler and override OnImageEvent. Keep a reference to the handler on self — PySpin does not keep the Python object alive and a garbage-collected handler silently stops firing.

nodes.label: Pre-Roll Ring Buffer (2 s)
nodes.rationale: Runs whenever streaming, not just during trials, and is prepended on trial start so descent onset is never clipped by experimenter reaction time. ~23 MB per camera per 2 s at 720x540 Mono8 / 30 fps.

nodes.label: Decoupled Capture/Encode/Display Threading Model
nodes.rationale: Image event handler not polling, bounded per-camera queue that drops and counts on overflow, separate writer thread piping to FFmpeg stdin, preview throttled to ~15 fps reading latest-frame. Recording integrity must never depend on the GUI thread or any pose component.

nodes.label: Original Acquisition GUI Prompt (v3)
nodes.rationale: The originating spec that acquisition/CLAUDE.md was distilled from. Its hardware figures (720p60, ~110 MB pre-roll, ~75 MB/min, ~225 MB per 3-minute trial, CRF ~18) were later corrected by HARDWARE.md's measurement of a 720x540 sensor.

nodes.label: Copy GetNDArray() Before the Frame Escapes
nodes.norm_label: copy getndarray() before the frame escapes
nodes.rationale: GetNDArray() returns a view onto a buffer the SDK recycles at Release(); frames outlive the callback (pre-roll deque ~60, writer queue up to 120) so a view would alias data the camera already overwrote. Corruption scales with queue depth and looks like a compression artifact — the highest-risk line in the file.

nodes.label: Incomplete Frames Counted Separately From Dropped Frames
nodes.norm_label: incomplete frames counted separately from dropped frames
nodes.rationale: A full queue means the encoder cannot keep up; an incomplete image means the camera-to-host link dropped data. Different causes, different fixes, so they never share a counter — hence CameraBackend.incomplete_frame_count.

nodes.label: Invariant 3 — Capture Never Blocks
nodes.rationale: One capture thread per camera using Spinnaker's image event handler (not polling) feeding a bounded queue and a separate writer thread; on queue-full drop the frame, increment a counter and log, never block.

nodes.label: Checkpoint A11 — Application Wiring (Composition Root)
nodes.rationale: Every part is built and tested but nothing outside tests constructs a camera, CaptureController, CameraRig or screen; app/__main__.py raises NotImplementedError. This composition root is what stands between the repo and lab use.

nodes.label: Checkpoint Protocol
nodes.rationale: State the ID and done-when criterion, implement, test, run pytest, commit on pass or commit as '(tests failing)' with a diagnosis on failure and move on. Never stall, never delete or weaken a test to make it pass, never leave uncommitted work at a checkpoint boundary.

nodes.label: Behavioral Video Acquisition GUI
nodes.rationale: Replaces SpinView, which requires manual start/stop and post-hoc association of video files with animal metadata; this app binds metadata at write time and reduces per-trial interaction to a single keypress.

nodes.label: Monorepo Layout (shared/schema + acquisition + analysis)
nodes.rationale: Two independent applications are kept in one repo so the only shared code, shared/schema/, can be the enforced contract between them; app-specific code stays inside its own subdirectory.

nodes.label: Overnight Build Report
nodes.rationale: A0–A9 and B1–B7 all complete with 200 passing tests (81 acquisition, 113 analysis, 6 shared) requiring zero hardware, GPU, DeepLabCut or network. Unattended-run discipline was kept even though the run was interactive, because it produces an auditable, resumable trail either way.

nodes.label: QUESTIONS.md — Unattended Ambiguity Log
nodes.rationale: One entry per ambiguity recording file, decision faced, options, choice and why, always implemented as the most conservative interpretation, so an unattended run leaves an auditable and resumable trail instead of silent guesses.

nodes.label: Unattended Run Discipline
nodes.rationale: Because nobody can answer questions, ambiguities go to QUESTIONS.md with the most conservative interpretation implemented and marked `# TODO(QUESTIONS.md): <ref>`; invariants are never relaxed to make something work; scope is never expanded; no system software installs, history rewrites, or force-pushes.

nodes.label: acquisition/acquisition/ Package Naming Collision
nodes.rationale: acquisition/CLAUDE.md's project structure names the capture-internals package `acquisition/`, which nested inside the monorepo's own acquisition app directory reads as acquisition/acquisition/camera_backend.py. Kept exactly as specified rather than guessing at a rename; the block was probably written for a standalone single-purpose repo.

nodes.rationale: Inserts between stages 7 and 8. Schemas are designed view-tagged and long-format now so this is an inserted stage rather than a rewrite. Do not build yet.

nodes.label: FFmpeg LGPL v2.1 Compliance Notice
nodes.rationale: Records that FFmpeg is used under LGPL v2.1 and pins the exact upstream commit (5156578d1f486163d5b83f1d63246cd23d107933) so the corresponding source is identifiable — the same LGPL reasoning that makes PySide6 rather than PyQt5 the GUI choice.

nodes.label: Encoder Tuning Lever Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Ordered by how much each actually matters: exposure time (motion blur destroys keypoint precision and no bitrate recovers it) > resolution/ROI > crf/qsv_global_quality > preset > codec choice. Measure with tools/measure_encoder.py rather than guessing; SSIM is only a proxy for keypoint accuracy.

nodes.label: Single-Camera Kinematics Are Provisional
nodes.rationale: Rats spiral around the pole, so with one lateral camera the animal is occluded behind the pole for a meaningful fraction of every trial. Also, snout, centroid and tail base are separated along the height axis, so keypoint choice changes the shape of the velocity profile rather than adding a constant offset.

nodes.label: A9.5 · encoder quality scales were shared (RESOLVED)
nodes.norm_label: a9.5 · encoder quality scales were shared (resolved)
nodes.rationale: One crf key fed both codecs while -crf and -global_quality are different scales, so recorded quality silently depended on which encoder resolved on that machine — files from a QSV machine and an x264 machine were not comparable when pooled into one DLC training set. Split into crf and qsv_global_quality with per-codec preset; qsv_global_quality falls back to crf so older configs still load.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.close()
nodes.rationale: DeInit, del the CameraPtr, Clear the CameraList, then ReleaseInstance only at zero open cameras. Always tears down including on error paths so this app never becomes the thing that leaves the camera latched for the next run.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.load_user_set()
nodes.rationale: Checks PySpin.IsWritable() on the command node before executing and returns False with a clear log line rather than letting an AccessException escape; preflight, not the backend, decides whether a load failure blocks.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.verify_settings()
nodes.rationale: Strictly read-only — never write a node to make a check pass, which is what keeps invariant 7 intact. An absent or unreadable node is a failed NodeCheck with actual '<unreadable>', not an exception. Float nodes compared as strings would be brittle, so the numeric frame-rate check is done separately by preflight against capture.fps_tolerance.

nodes.label: Preflight Checks
nodes.rationale: Config is not ground truth about hardware — it is intent; the backend reports actuals and preflight compares. Does not short-circuit on first failure so an experimenter with an animal in hand sees everything wrong in one pass. A 1280x720 config value meeting a 720x540 sensor silently sheared video with no error.

nodes.label: A10 · read-only nodes misdiagnosed as camera fault (CORRECTED)
nodes.norm_label: a10 · read-only nodes misdiagnosed as camera fault (corrected)
nodes.rationale: A9.5 recorded the RO nodes as a possible firmware fault, reasoning from DeviceAccessStatus, StreamIsGrabbing and TLParamsLocked — all host-side state for the probing process, none able to observe another process holding the camera. Actual cause was a live Spinnaker session. Cost: one round of misdirected hardware troubleshooting, no code rework.

nodes.label: PDCT (Pole Descent Cognitive Test)
nodes.rationale: Rats descend a vertical pole; trials run 1-5 minutes, long relative to mouse PDCT, so every duration threshold is a config value rather than a literal.

nodes.label: y(t) — Trustworthy Scaled Vertical Position Series
nodes.norm_label: y(t) — trustworthy scaled vertical position series
nodes.rationale: The pipeline's actual product. Descent time is a trivial query against y(t); the height-resolved velocity profile is the novel measurement and cannot be obtained any other way, so every stage is designed to serve y(t) accuracy.

nodes.label: Paradigm Plugin Seam (PDCTParadigm only)
nodes.rationale: A Paradigm abstraction covers metadata schema, trial state machine and output naming, with exactly one concrete implementation shipped; the seam makes adding a maze paradigm a matter of writing a new class rather than touching the acquisition core.

nodes.label: PDCT Analysis Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Config-driven, scriptable, CLI-only pipeline replacing ad-hoc notebooks and the DLC GUI, which are neither reproducible nor batchable. Has no PySpin dependency and never touches camera hardware.

nodes.label: Invariant 9 — Config Over Literals
nodes.rationale: Durations, thresholds, keymaps, paths and encoder settings all live in TOML so a second rig or a new paradigm needs no source change.

nodes.label: Invariant 5 — Every Artifact Carries Provenance
nodes.rationale: A .provenance.json sidecar records input artifact hashes, config hash, code commit, DLC snapshot ID, stage version and timestamp — which is also what makes invariant 4's skip-when-hashes-match idempotency possible.

nodes.label: Spinnaker Chunk Data (FrameID + Timestamp)
nodes.rationale: Per-frame metadata embedded by the camera; the app must enable ChunkModeActive and both chunks itself because the camera ships with them off and invariant 6 is otherwise unsatisfiable.

nodes.label: Invariant 6 — Hardware Timestamps Only
nodes.rationale: Chunk timestamps and frame IDs go to a per-trial CSV sidecar; host wall-clock arrival time is never substituted because future ephys alignment and 3D triangulation depend on camera-side time.

nodes.label: Invariant 12 — Analysis fps Decoupled from Acquisition fps
nodes.norm_label: invariant 12 — analysis fps decoupled from acquisition fps
nodes.rationale: Any temporal downsampling is an explicit, logged config choice; conflating the two would let a downsampling setting silently corrupt capture-rate QC.

nodes.label: B3 · qc.nominal_fps as its own config key
nodes.norm_label: b3 · qc.nominal_fps as its own config key
nodes.rationale: Reusing analysis.fps would couple two concepts invariant 12 says must stay decoupled: setting analysis.fps to downsample kinematics would make every trial fail QC for fps deviation even though nothing about the capture changed. Added qc.nominal_fps (default 30.0, matching acquisition's capture.fps).

nodes.label: Stage 6 · evaluate
nodes.rationale: Per-keypoint error matters because static pole landmarks should be near-zero — high error there means the coordinate frame itself is unreliable. Acts as a gate: batch inference must not run if error exceeds the config threshold.

nodes.label: Stage 3 · extract_frames
nodes.rationale: Stratified across animal × date × session so no single animal or lighting condition dominates, with a motion/ROI prefilter before k-means because blind k-means wastes labelling budget on uninformative and occluded frames. Frame provenance back to source trial is mandatory so a bad label is traceable.

nodes.label: Stage 4 · labeling (manual)
nodes.rationale: Keypoint scheme lives in config as single source of truth and must include static pole landmarks. Label snout, mid-back/centroid and tail base so primary_keypoint can be compared without re-labelling. Never trim a SuperAnimal keypoint set to a subset — fine-tuning to a reduced subset behaves unexpectedly.

nodes.label: Open Experimental-Design Decisions
nodes.rationale: SuperAnimal zero-shot comparison, primary_keypoint choice, descent onset/offset rule parameters, QC thresholds and filter windows, cu128 verification — recorded rather than resolved unattended because they are experimental-design choices, and primary_keypoint criteria must be fixed before looking at group differences.

nodes.label: Stage 5 · train
nodes.rationale: SuperAnimal initialisation; Quadruped is the expected init for lateral views because subjects are rats, while TopViewMouse is mouse-trained so top-down init must be decided by zero-shot comparison rather than assumption.

nodes.label: Shared PySpin System Singleton
nodes.rationale: System.GetInstance() is process-wide, so with N cameras each instance must share one System behind a reference-counted, lock-guarded module-level singleton. Releasing while another camera is open is a classic PySpin crash; CameraPtr and CameraList must be explicitly del'd before ReleaseInstance().

nodes.label: Invariant 1 — N-Camera by Construction
nodes.rationale: Cameras come from a config list currently holding one entry; two more views (lateral, top-down) arrive later and must not force a refactor.

nodes.label: Manual Release of CameraPtr / CameraList / SystemPtr
nodes.norm_label: manual release of cameraptr / cameralist / systemptr
nodes.rationale: CameraPtr, CameraList, InterfacePtr, InterfaceList and SystemPtr must be manually released and/or deleted before program exit using the del operator — the SDK does not clean them up on scope exit the way the C++ objects do.

nodes.label: Trial State Machine (IDLE → RECORDING → IDLE)
nodes.rationale: min_trial_duration_s swallows double-tap zero-length trials; suspicious_duration_s auto-flags implausibly fast descents; max_trial_duration_s auto-stops so an animal that never descends cannot run away with the disk.

nodes.label: A3 · min-duration guard vs. predicate stop
nodes.norm_label: a3 · min-duration guard vs. predicate stop
nodes.rationale: Applied the min-duration swallow guard uniformly to manual and predicate-triggered stops: most conservative, never produces a trial shorter than min_trial_duration_s, and inert today because KeypressStopCondition never self-triggers.

nodes.label: PySpin NumPy 2.x Incompatibility Notice
nodes.rationale: Vendor confirmation that PySpin does not support NumPy 2.x — the upstream source the acquisition requirements.txt upper bound cites.

nodes.label: numpy<2 Upper Bound (acquisition)
nodes.rationale: PySpin does not support numpy 2.x; unbounded, a fresh install pulls 2.x and `import PySpin` stops working, so the upper bound is load-bearing rather than cautious.

nodes.label: FLIR Camera Getting Started (empty file)
nodes.rationale: Zero-byte placeholder in the vendor docs directory; intended content is presumably FLIR's getting-started guide but nothing can be extracted from it.

nodes.label: PySpin vs C++ API Differences
nodes.rationale: INode/IValue returned from GetNode() must be cast to their pointer types (CFloatPtr, CEnumerationPtr) before use; GetNDArray() returns a 2- or 3-D NumPy array only for select formats; node callbacks take a callback class rather than a function pointer.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.stop_streaming()
nodes.rationale: EndAcquisition() before UnregisterEventHandler() — the reverse order has caused crashes in past Spinnaker versions. Idempotent when not streaming.
